newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FOTEX TO ISSUE CONVERTIBLE BONDS.
newsitem.headline: FOTEX TO ISSUE CONVERTIBLE BONDS.

text.p: The shareholders of the Hungarian retail company Fotex decided on Tuesday that the company should issue convertible bonds worth $20 million in four equal tranches from November this year to April, 1998.
The bonds, which could be converted into shares after the three-year maturity, will be sold at a price equal to the $8,000 face value which each bonds have, to Fotex shareholders.
"This is a sufficiently attractive proposition to shareholders for them to consider this a meaningful investment," Fotex Chairman Gabor Varszegi told the shareholders.

The first bond issue is scheduled to take place between November 20 and December 20 this year, the second from April 1 to 30, 1997, the third from September 1 to 30, 1997, and the fourth from April 1-30, 1998, Varszegi said.
The bonds will pay fixed interest of between eight and 12 percent in dollars and the interest rate will be set by the board before each issue.
The private placement is open only to foreign shareholders.
After three years each bond may be converted into 10,000 registered ordinary shares with nominal value of 100 forints each.
Holders of the bonds must declare whether they want to convert the bonds into shares 30 days before the bonds mature.

"The issue will raise 20 million dollars in three and a half years," Varszegi said. "Our goal is to preserve Fotex's position in the Hungarian retail market and to increase the value of the company in general."
Varszegi said the company planned to use the new capital to open retail outlets in the new generation of shopping malls which are expected to open in Hungary over the next few years.
Fotex already has outlets in the first of such centres, the $55-million Duna Plaza in Budapest, which opened its doors last month.
